record.original_question: Let X be the smooth 4-manifold underlying a complex K3 surface and let T be an embedded torus in X with trivial normal bundle. For a knot K in S^3, let X_K be the Fintushel-Stern knot-surgery 4-manifold obtained by cutting out a neighbourhood of T and gluing in the product of S^1 with the complement of a tubular neighbourhood of K. If knots K1 and K2 have the same Alexander polynomial, must X_K1 and X_K2 be diffeomorphic?

evidence.quote: It is easy to construct distinct knots with same Alexander polynomial, so our question becomes the following: if K1, K2 are knots with the same Alexander polynomial, are the 4-manifolds XK1 , XK2 diffeomorphic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be the smooth $4$-manifold underlying a complex K3 surface, and let $T \subset X$ be a smoothly embedded $2$-torus with trivial normal bundle. For any knot $K \subset S^3$, let $
u(K)$ denote an open tubular neighborhood of $K$, and let $
u(T)$ denote an open tubular neighborhood of $T$ (so $
u(T) \cong T^2 	imes D^2$). The Fintushel–Stern knot-surgery $4$-manifold is defined by
$$X_K \;=\;  igl(X \setminus 
u(T) igr) \;\cup_\varphi\;  igl(S^1 	imes (S^3 \setminus 
u(K)) igr),$$
where the gluing diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of the boundary $3$-tori is chosen so that the homology class of a meridian of $T$ is identified with the class of $S^1 	imes \lambda_K$, where $\lambda_K$ denotes a longitude of $K$.

Question: If $K_1$ and $K_2$ are knots in $S^3$ with equal Alexander polynomials $\Delta_{K_1}(t) = \Delta_{K_2}(t)$, must the smooth $4$-manifolds $X_{K_1}$ and $X_{K_2}$ be diffeomorphic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a well-known open problem in 4-manifold topology. The Seiberg–Witten invariants of $X_K$ depend only on the Alexander polynomial of $K$, so they cannot distinguish $X_{K_1}$ from $X_{K_2}$ when the Alexander polynomials agree. Partial results show that for many families (e.g., certain fibered knots of the same genus with equal Alexander polynomial) the resulting 4-manifolds are indeed diffeomorphic, but no general proof or counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: Fintushel–Stern knot surgery in torus bundles
status_evidence.snippet: It is an interesting question whether the diffeomorphism type of the resulting 4-manifolds determines the knot type... infinitely many inequivalent genus g fibered knots (for g ≥ 2) sharing the same Alexander polynomial whose corresponding knot surgery 4-manifolds are all diffeomorphic.
status_evidence.claim: The general question remains open, while partial affirmative results exist for fibered knots.

status_evidence.title: Twisted fiber sums of Fintushel-Stern's knot surgery 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of knot surgery 4-manifolds and their invariants depending on Alexander polynomial.
status_evidence.claim: Standard SW invariants of $X_K$ depend only on $\Delta_K$, motivating the open question.
